question: A bowl contains 9 blue balls, 7 white and 5 black balls. If 2 balls are drawn in one go, then the probability of exactly one ball being white is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

We need exactly 1 white ball and 1 non-white ball from 21 total balls (7 white, 14 non-white).

Probability = P(First is White, Second is Non-White) + P(First is Non-White, Second is White)

P = (7/21 × 14/20) + (14/21 × 7/20)

P = (1/3 × 7/10) + (2/3 × 7/20)

P = 7/30 + 7/30 = 14/30 = 7/15

**∴ The correct answer is 7/15.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Number of blue balls = 9

Number of white balls = 7

Number of black balls = 5

Number of balls drawn = 2

**Formula Used:**

Probability = Number of Favorable Outcomes ÷ Total Possible Outcomes

Combination formula: ⁿCᵣ = n! ÷ [r! × (n−r)!]

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total number of balls = 9 + 7 + 5 = 21

⇒ Total possible outcomes when drawing 2 balls = ²¹C₂

⇒ ²¹C₂ = (21 × 20) ÷ (2 × 1) = 210

⇒ Number of non-white balls = 9 (blue) + 5 (black) = 14

⇒ We need exactly one white ball, which implies drawing 1 white ball AND 1 non-white ball.

⇒ Number of favorable outcomes = ⁷C₁ × ¹⁴C₁

⇒ Favorable outcomes = 7 × 14 = 98

⇒ Required Probability = 98 ÷ 210

⇒ Divide numerator and denominator by 14: 98 ÷ 14 = 7 and 210 ÷ 14 = 15

⇒ Required Probability = 7/15

**∴ The correct answer is 7/15.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Combinations in Probability

When drawing multiple items simultaneously, combinations (ⁿCᵣ) are used to find the number of ways to select r items from a total of n items without regard to order.

Mutually Exclusive Events

Events that cannot occur at the same time. The probability of either event A or event B occurring is the sum of their individual probabilities: P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B).

Multiplication Rule for Dependent Events

When drawing items one after another without replacement, the outcome of the first draw affects the probabilities of the second draw: P(A and B) = P(A) × P(B after A).
